profile.headline: Software Engineer at Roblox
profile.summary:
I am currently a Software Engineer at Roblox as a fresh 2020 graduate from Carnegie Mellon University, with a degree in Statistics and Machine Learning and an additional major in Computer Science.

My previous experiences were internships, which was building a Machine Learning algorithm to predict how long a job will wait in a queue at Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center, and optimizing data generation for canary testing at Amazon.

I am more than happy to talk about my experiences or listen to your experiences in more detail!

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description:
Designed and implemented a multi-threading solution to optimize data generation for canaries. Canaries monitor service health by calling APIs regularly

Reduced data generation latency from 10 hours to 10 minutes, helping our team roll out their services to new regions faster 

Automated creation of data generation infrastructure (S3 Bucket) by using a Continuous Deployment framework

positions.title: AI/Big Data Intern
positions.description: My time in Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center really helped me to get a first taste in the field of Machine Learning. Before even thinking about Machine Learning models, I first had to learn about the ins and outs of a supercomputer and explore the systems that stored and transferred data. Afterwards, I had to really get to know my data, and spent days creating data visualizations. Finally, I got to the fun part: building models for predicting queue wait times for jobs. I used the pyTorch library to build a neural network, again spending days testing and debugging my model to finally get a complete product, which I presented in front of the entire company.

positions.title: Reserach Assistant
positions.description: When I came to the Human-Computer Interaction Institute at CMU to discuss research opportunities, I did not really have much experience in my belt, apart from the few classes that I had taken in my first year. My mentor was very helpful and patient, explaining that the research project explored the potential for humans to learn optimal strategies for a racing computer game. This sounded exciting, so I was immediately on board, using my python knowledge that I had picked up from my intro to programming class in order to extract thousands of random game sessions and performance metrics from OpenAI Gym, and also implemented a Mini-Batch K-Means Clustering algorithm using scikit-learn to approximate an optimal game strategy, serving as a benchmark for computer-level performance. Lastly, I tested all functions using visualizations from matplotlib to ensure correctness of my data analysis.
